title: Bodies, Consent, Online Life & the Loud Myths

myths.myth: There's one ideal body type.
myths.truth: Healthy bodies come in many shapes and sizes.
myths.explanation: Diversity is the norm; a single 'ideal' is the myth.

myths.myth: Edited photos online show how people really look.
myths.truth: Most images are filtered, posed or edited.
myths.explanation: Comparing yourself to edits is unfair to you.

myths.myth: Your worth depends on your looks.
myths.truth: You're worth far more than your appearance.
myths.explanation: Character, kindness and skills matter most.

myths.myth: Acne, body hair and changes are flaws to hide.
myths.truth: They're a normal part of growing up.
myths.explanation: Everyone goes through it — there's no shame in it.

myths.myth: Resilience means never feeling down.
myths.truth: It means coping and bouncing back.
myths.explanation: Everyone falls; recovering is the actual skill.

myths.myth: Real strength is hiding your struggles.
myths.truth: Naming a struggle and asking for help is strength.
myths.explanation: Bottling things up only makes them heavier.

myths.myth: If you fail at something, you're a failure.
myths.truth: Failing at a thing doesn't make you a failure.
myths.explanation: Setbacks are how we learn and grow.

myths.myth: You should just 'be positive'.
myths.truth: All feelings are okay; coping skills help.
myths.explanation: Forced positivity ignores what you really feel.

myths.myth: You can't get pregnant the 'first time'.
myths.truth: Pregnancy is possible whenever sperm meets egg.
myths.explanation: Myths like this lead to real risks; facts protect you.

myths.myth: Contraception is only the girl's job.
myths.truth: Preventing pregnancy is a shared responsibility.
myths.explanation: It takes both partners — and honest conversation.

myths.myth: Talking about contraception is shameful.
myths.truth: Knowing your options is responsible.
myths.explanation: Information protects health and futures.

myths.myth: Withdrawal or 'safe days' always work.
myths.truth: They're unreliable; reliable methods exist.
myths.explanation: Knowing the facts lets you make safe choices later.

myths.myth: You can tell if someone has an STI by looking.
myths.truth: Most STIs have no visible signs.
myths.explanation: That's exactly why testing and protection matter.

myths.myth: STIs only happen to certain 'types' of people.
myths.truth: Anyone can get an STI.
myths.explanation: Infections don't discriminate.

myths.myth: An STI is a punishment to be ashamed of.
myths.truth: They're health conditions, and often treatable.
myths.explanation: Shame stops people getting the care they need.

myths.myth: No symptoms means nothing to worry about.
myths.truth: Many STIs are silent; testing still matters.
myths.explanation: Early care protects you and others.

myths.myth: Consent is just one yes at the start.
myths.truth: Consent is ongoing, enthusiastic and can be withdrawn.
myths.explanation: Checking in is part of respect, not a mood-killer.

myths.myth: Pressuring or guilt-tripping is normal in relationships.
myths.truth: That's a red flag, not love.
myths.explanation: Healthy relationships never run on pressure.

myths.myth: Jealousy and control show how much someone loves you.
myths.truth: They're warning signs.
myths.explanation: Trust, not control, is the green light.

myths.myth: If you're dating, you owe each other things.
myths.truth: No one owes anyone their body.
myths.explanation: You can always say no — at any point.

myths.myth: There are only rigid 'boy' and 'girl' ways to be.
myths.truth: Gender is broader than the stereotypes.
myths.explanation: People express who they are in many ways.

myths.myth: Boys don't have feelings and shouldn't cry.
myths.truth: All genders feel deeply.
myths.explanation: Suppressing feelings harms everyone.

myths.myth: Girls aren't suited to STEM or leadership.
myths.truth: Ability isn't gendered.
myths.explanation: Stereotypes — not talent — hold people back.

myths.myth: Equality means everyone being the same.
myths.truth: It means equal rights and respect, honouring difference.
myths.explanation: Fairness isn't sameness.

myths.myth: Men lose when women gain.
myths.truth: Equality benefits everyone.
myths.explanation: It isn't a zero-sum game.

myths.myth: Some inequality is just 'natural'.
myths.truth: Most inequality is built by rules and norms.
myths.explanation: What's built by people can be changed by people.

myths.myth: Harassment is just joking around.
myths.truth: Unwanted comments and touching are harassment.
myths.explanation: Impact matters more than someone's 'intent'.

myths.myth: It's not your business if it's happening to someone else.
myths.truth: Safe bystanders can help.
myths.explanation: Standing up (safely) can stop harm.

myths.myth: People provoke harassment by how they dress or act.
myths.truth: Harassment is the harasser's choice.
myths.explanation: It's never the victim's fault.

myths.myth: Sending a private photo is harmless if you trust them.
myths.truth: Once sent, you lose control of an image.
myths.explanation: Think before you share — and you can always say no.

myths.myth: People online are who they claim to be.
myths.truth: Grooming often starts with fake friendliness.
myths.explanation: Be cautious; tell a trusted adult if you're pressured.

myths.myth: If you started a chat, you can't back out.
myths.truth: You can stop, block and report any time.
myths.explanation: You're never trapped in an online conversation.

myths.myth: Cyberbullying isn't 'real' bullying.
myths.truth: Online harm is real harm.
myths.explanation: Save the evidence and get help.

myths.myth: Influencers who 'tell hard truths' about men and women are just honest.
myths.truth: Many profit from anger and division.
myths.explanation: Outrage drives clicks — it isn't the same as truth.

myths.myth: Feminism is about women beating men.
myths.truth: It's about equal rights for all genders.
myths.explanation: Distorted definitions are designed to fuel resentment.

myths.myth: A 'real man' means dominance and never showing weakness.
myths.truth: Real strength includes respect and emotion.
myths.explanation: Rigid scripts harm boys, too.

myths.myth: If a video confirms what you feel, it must be right.
myths.truth: Algorithms feed you more of what hooks you.
myths.explanation: Question the feed, not just the world.

myths.myth: What you see in media (or porn) is how real intimacy works.
myths.truth: It's staged performance, not real life.
myths.explanation: Real relationships run on consent and communication.

myths.myth: If lots of people share it, it must be true.
myths.truth: Popular doesn't mean accurate.
myths.explanation: Misinformation spreads fast.

myths.myth: Ads and influencers just want to help you.
myths.truth: They're usually selling something.
myths.explanation: Knowing the motive protects you.

myths.myth: You can't do anything about misinformation.
myths.truth: You can check sources and think critically.
myths.explanation: A 'reality check' is a skill you can build.
